title: Suspension Alignment and Ride-Height Specifications
introduction:
I start with the Mustang's exact body style and package before reading an alignment row. These tables distinguish front and rear settings, individual sides and combined or split values; similar-looking model names do not make their settings interchangeable.

Camber is wheel tilt viewed from the front or rear, while toe describes wheel direction viewed from above. Think of them as separate adjustments to the tire's handshake with the road. Use the printed units and tolerances, and apply the stated curb-load condition to alignment and ride height. This is a specification reference; measurement points, equipment setup and adjustment procedures belong to the matching service instructions.

edits.why: Select the front or rear section, then the row matching the body style, package and model. LH and RH identify the left and right sides. Read Total/Split with the relevant item: total toe combines the sides, while split describes the side-to-side difference. Preserve the printed signs and tolerances; a dash supplies no individual value.

edits.text: NOTE: These alignment specifications apply at curb load: full service fluids, full fuel tank(s), no passengers and no cargo.
edits.why: The loading condition is part of the specification. I establish it before comparing measurements so passenger or cargo weight does not become an uninvited alignment adjustment.

Choose the correct axle section and model row, and keep the nominal height paired with its printed tolerance. The rear nominal parenthetical values omit a unit label; the metric values are explicitly labeled. The measurement locations are not defined here, so these figures do not establish where to place a measuring tool.

edits.text: NOTE: These ride-height specifications apply at curb load: full service fluids, full fuel tank(s), no passengers and no cargo.
edits.why: Ride height must be compared under the specified loading condition. A loaded car and an unloaded reference are answering different questions.

These are maximum side-to-side differences, with separate front and rear limits. They are not additional nominal ride heights. Use the matching vehicle-lean measurement procedure to establish the comparison points.
The following rear thrust-angle row applies to all models. Keep this angle separate from the individual rear-wheel camber and toe entries; its printed tolerance belongs to its own measurement.
